# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Fornari_2019_carboplatin_rat"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12459> (open access, PMC6875710)
* Packaged models:
  * `Fornari_2019_carboplatin_rat` -- the model fitted to rat bone marrow
    and blood data.
  * `Fornari_2019_carboplatin_human` -- the authors' translation of the same
    structure to patients (a prediction, not a fit to human data).

Fornari et al. built a quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) model of
haematopoiesis that links free-platinum pharmacokinetics after carboplatin to
DNA damage in proliferating bone marrow progenitors and, through lineage-
specific maturation chains and cross-lineage feedback, to circulating
neutrophils, monocytes, reticulocytes, platelets and red blood cells. The
model was fitted to six rat studies and then translated to humans by swapping
physiology-dependent parameters and scaling the drug-sensitivity slopes by
in vitro IC50 ratios.

# Population

The rat model was fitted to 178 male RccHan:WIST rats (about 12 weeks old,
at least 320 g) from six AstraZeneca studies (Table S1): single IV doses of
3, 10, 30 or 40 mg/kg carboplatin, or 40 mg/kg every 14 days for up to eight
cycles, with vehicle controls. Haematology was measured on a Siemens Advia
2120i; femur bone marrow multipotent progenitors (MPP, CD90+/Lin-), common
myeloid progenitors (CMP, CD45+) and megakaryocyte-erythrocyte progenitors
(MEP, CD71+) by flow cytometry; free platinum in plasma ultrafiltrate by
UPLC-MS/MS (Supplementary Text S1-S4). PK and PD were fitted sequentially
with naive pooling, so the model has no between-animal variability.

The human model was not fitted to data. Its predictions (Figure 4) were for
patients dosed by the Calvert formula to an AUC of 5 mg*min/mL with a GFR of
125 mL/min, over two 21-day cycles.

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Fornari_2019_carboplatin_rat"))$population)
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Fornari_2019_carboplatin_human"))$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. The table
collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Rat | Human | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free-platinum PK `cl`, `vc`, `vp`, `q` | 0.42 L/h, 0.26 L, 0.30 L, 0.06 L/h | 7.2 L/h, 15.5 L, 9.86 L, 3.46 L/h | Rat: Table S3, Equation S1. Human: Zandvliet 2008 Table 2 (Supplementary Text S11), CL at CLcr 125 mL/min |
| DNA damage `kdam`, `krep` | 0.017, 0.017 1/h | as rat | Table 1; Equation 3 |
| `kcirc_anc`, `kcirc_mono`, `kcirc_plt`, `kcirc_rbc` | 0.17, 0.06, 0.01, 0.0007 1/h | 0.1, 0.04, 0.0052, 0.00037 1/h | Table 1 |
| Baselines Neut0, Mono0, Plt0, Ret0, RBC0 | 1.32, 0.16, 967, 235, 8161 | 4.5, 0.6, 345, 77.5, 5000 | Table 1 (human: midpoints of printed ranges for Neut0, Mono0, Ret0, RBC0) |
| Baselines MPP0, CMP0, MEP0 | 69, 214, 156 | 1.3, 20.9, 15 | Table 1; Equations S8-S9 |
| MTT Neut, Mono, Plt, Ret | 61.5, 62.2, 74, 75 h | 210, 121.5, 168, 66 h | Table 1 |
| lambda1-lambda5 | 2, 2, 1.8, 1.8, 1.8 | as rat | Table 1; Equation S7 |
| gamma stem, MatCMP, MatMEP, prolTrans | 0.07, 0.6, 0.3, 0.7 | as rat | Table 1; Equations 11-13 |
| SlopeMPP, SlopeCMP, SlopeMEP | 2.05, 1.47, 2.19 1/uM | 0.79, 0.57, 0.66 1/uM | Table 2 |
| deltaRet, deltaPlt | 2.8, 0.54 | as rat | Table 2 |
| Log-additive residual SDs | 0.33, 0.19, 0.33, 0.17, 0.17, 0.17, 0.36, 0.06 | carried from rat | Table S4 (MPP, CMP, MEP, Neut, Mono, Plt, Ret, RBC) |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)` | | | Equation S1 |
| `d/dt(damage)` | | | Equation 3 |
| `d/dt(mpp)`, `d/dt(cmp)`, `d/dt(mep)` | | | Equations 1, 2, 4 |
| Neutrophil and monocyte transit chains | | | Equations 5-6 |
| Reticulocyte and platelet transit chains | | | Equations 7-8 |
| Circulating neutrophils, monocytes, reticulocytes, platelets | | | Equation 9 |
| `d/dt(circ_rbc)` and `kcirc_ret` | | | Equation S4 (`kcircRet = kcircRBC * RBC0 / Ret0`) |
| Feedback functions | | | Equations 11-13 (weights 1/2 = `alphaWBC` in the model code) |
| Steady-state rates `ktr_*`, `kprol_*`, `kstem` and initial conditions | | | Equations S2-S4, S7 |

# Homeostasis

All differentiation and proliferation rates are derived from the untreated
steady state (Equations S3-S4), so without drug every state must stay at its
baseline. This checks the transcription of the steady-state algebra, which
any error in one of the eighteen rate expressions would break.

```{r homeostasis}
mod_rat <- readModelDb("Fornari_2019_carboplatin_rat")
mod_hum <- readModelDb("Fornari_2019_carboplatin_human")
outputs <- c("MPP", "CMP", "MEP", "ANC", "MONO", "PLT", "RET", "RBC")

# Observation rows of a model with several error-model endpoints carry the
# ODE state in `cmt` and `dvid = 1`; rxSolve then returns every output column.
obs_rows <- function(times) {
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = times, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
}
dose_rows <- function(times, amt, rate = 0) {
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = times, amt = amt, rate = rate, evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_)
}

drift <- function(mod) {
  s <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod, obs_rows(seq(0, 2000, by = 100)), rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12))
  vapply(outputs, function(v) max(abs(s[[v]] / s[[v]][1] - 1)), numeric(1))
}
hold <- rbind(rat = drift(mod_rat), human = drift(mod_hum))
knitr::kable(signif(hold, 2), caption = "Largest relative drift from baseline over 2000 h without drug.")
stopifnot(all(hold < 1e-6))
```

# Rat free-platinum PK and DNA damage (Figure S3)

Figure S3 shows the PK fit to 20 mg/kg (Siddik 1987) and 30 mg/kg (in-house)
free-platinum data and the DNA damage it drives. The maintainers digitised
the plotted PK and damage curves; the plot's dosing time is 24 h, shifted to
0 here.

```{r figS3}
pk_ev <- function(dose, subject) {
  rbind(dose_rows(0, dose), obs_rows(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.05), seq(2.25, 24, by = 0.25)))) |>
    mutate(id = subject, treatment = paste(dose, "mg/kg"))
}
# One solve per dose level: the model has no IIV, so a multi-subject solve
# only adds an rxode2 warning.
sim_pk <- bind_rows(lapply(1:2, function(i) {
  ev <- pk_ev(c(20, 30)[i], i)
  as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod_rat, ev)) |> mutate(id = i, treatment = ev$treatment[1])
}))
# One subject per dose level: the solve must return both, and the 30 mg/kg
# peak is dose / Vc converted to uM (30 / 0.26 * 1000 / 371.25 = 311 uM).
stopifnot(
  setequal(unique(sim_pk$id), 1:2),
  abs(max(sim_pk$Cc[sim_pk$treatment == "30 mg/kg"]) / (30 / 0.26 * 1000 / 371.25) - 1) < 1e-3
)

# Digitised from Figure S3 (blue PK line and orange damage line).
figS3_pk <- data.frame(
  time = c(1.32, 1.86, 2.39, 3.45, 8.77, 16.76, 23.68),
  Cc = c(49.0, 21.1, 10.6, 4.87, 1.63, 0.402, 0.119)
)
figS3_damage <- data.frame(time = c(3.5, 20.77), damage = c(4.77, 3.73))

ggplot(sim_pk, aes(time, Cc, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = figS3_pk, aes(time, Cc), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 1) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Free platinum (uM)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Open circles: plotted model line of Figure S3 (digitised). Replicates Figure S3 of Fornari 2019.")

ggplot(sim_pk, aes(time, damage, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = figS3_damage, aes(time, damage), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Damage (uM-equivalent)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Open circles: plotted damage line of Figure S3 (digitised).")

sim30 <- filter(sim_pk, treatment == "30 mg/kg")
ratio <- figS3_pk |>
  mutate(
    Cc_sim = approx(sim30$time, sim30$Cc, xout = time)$y,
    fig_over_sim = Cc / Cc_sim
  ) |>
  rename(Cc_fig = Cc)
knitr::kable(select(ratio, time, Cc_sim, Cc_fig, fig_over_sim), digits = 3,
             caption = "30 mg/kg: packaged model vs the plotted Figure S3 line.")
```

The packaged model reproduces the shape of the Figure S3 line exactly, but
the plotted line sits about 1.5-fold above the 30 mg/kg simulation at every
time (see Assumptions and deviations). The simulation at 30 mg/kg agrees with
the plotted 30 mg/kg observations (about 120-250 uM at 15 min, about 50 uM at
1 h, 4-6 uM at 3 h, 0.07-0.09 uM at 24 h).

```{r figS3-check}
# A dose-unit or molar-mass error would scale every row by the same factor;
# the shape is fixed by Table S3, so the factor is constant across time.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(ratio$fig_over_sim) - 1.5) < 0.2,
  diff(range(ratio$fig_over_sim)) < 0.35
)
```

# Rat myelosuppression over eight cycles (Figure 3)

Figure 3 shows 40 mg/kg every 14 days. Its model lines show eight nadirs
(day 1 to day 99), matching the text's "eight cycles", so eight doses are
simulated here; Table S1 lists seven dosing days for study E. The bands are
the 5th-95th percentiles from the Table S4 log-additive residual error around
the typical prediction, which is how the paper's visual predictive check was
built.

```{r fig3}
dose_times <- seq(0, by = 336, length.out = 8)
ev_rat <- rbind(dose_rows(dose_times, 40), obs_rows(seq(0, 120 * 24, by = 4)))
sim_rat <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod_rat, ev_rat))

sig <- rxode2::rxode(mod_rat)$iniDf |>
  filter(grepl("^expSd_", name)) |>
  transmute(output = sub("^expSd_", "", name), sigma = est)

long_rat <- sim_rat |>
  select(time, all_of(outputs)) |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "output", values_to = "value") |>
  left_join(sig, by = "output") |>
  mutate(
    day = time / 24,
    lo = value * exp(qnorm(0.05) * sigma),
    hi = value * exp(qnorm(0.95) * sigma),
    output = factor(output, levels = outputs)
  )

ggplot(long_rat, aes(day, value)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~output, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "10^9 cells/L",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Fornari 2019 (40 mg/kg every 14 days).")
```

The maintainers read the model lines of Figure 3 (log axes, so the readings
are approximate) and compare them with the packaged model below.

```{r fig3-table}
cycle_stats <- lapply(seq_along(dose_times), function(k) {
  w <- sim_rat$time >= dose_times[k] & sim_rat$time < dose_times[k] + 336
  data.frame(
    cycle = k,
    MPP_min = min(sim_rat$MPP[w]), MPP_max = max(sim_rat$MPP[w]),
    MEP_min = min(sim_rat$MEP[w]),
    RET_min = min(sim_rat$RET[w]), RET_max = max(sim_rat$RET[w]),
    PLT_min = min(sim_rat$PLT[w]), PLT_max = max(sim_rat$PLT[w])
  )
}) |> bind_rows()
knitr::kable(cycle_stats, digits = 1, caption = "Per-cycle extremes of the packaged rat model.")

fig3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~quantity, ~figure_3, ~model,
  "MPP nadir (each cycle)", "about 8-9", sprintf("%.1f-%.1f", min(cycle_stats$MPP_min), max(cycle_stats$MPP_min)),
  "MPP peak, cycle 2 to cycle 8", "about 55 falling to about 43", sprintf("%.0f falling to %.0f", cycle_stats$MPP_max[2], cycle_stats$MPP_max[8]),
  "MEP nadir", "about 5", sprintf("%.1f", min(cycle_stats$MEP_min)),
  "Reticulocyte nadir", "about 13-15", sprintf("%.1f", min(cycle_stats$RET_min)),
  "Reticulocyte peak, cycles 2-8", "about 180-200", sprintf("%.0f-%.0f", min(cycle_stats$RET_max[-1]), max(cycle_stats$RET_max[-1])),
  "Platelet nadir", "about 230-250", sprintf("%.0f", min(cycle_stats$PLT_min)),
  "Platelet peak", "about 1000-1100", sprintf("%.0f", max(cycle_stats$PLT_max)),
  "Reticulocyte nadir, % below baseline (text)", "more than 95%", sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * (1 - min(sim_rat$RET) / sim_rat$RET[1])),
  "Peak rise of the stem-cell inflow (text)", "27%", sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * (max(sim_rat$fdbk_stem) - 1))
)
knitr::kable(fig3, caption = "Figure 3 and Results text vs the packaged rat model.")

stopifnot(
  # Progenitor depletion is set by SlopeMPP/SlopeMEP times the damage AUC;
  # a dose-unit error moves these by tens of percent.
  min(cycle_stats$MPP_min) > 7, max(cycle_stats$MPP_min) < 12,
  min(cycle_stats$MEP_min) > 3, min(cycle_stats$MEP_min) < 7,
  1 - min(sim_rat$RET) / sim_rat$RET[1] > 0.93,
  min(cycle_stats$PLT_min) > 180, min(cycle_stats$PLT_min) < 300,
  # The declining MPP peaks are the paper's evidence for the maturation feedback.
  cycle_stats$MPP_max[8] < cycle_stats$MPP_max[2]
)
```

Recovery after the last cycle, from the Results text: MEP needed 12 days,
MPP 30 days and CMP about 50 days to reinstate at least 80% of their original
population. The text does not say which reference time or level these were
measured from.

```{r recovery}
ev_rec <- rbind(dose_rows(dose_times, 40), obs_rows(seq(0, dose_times[8] + 150 * 24, by = 4)))
sim_rec <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod_rat, ev_rec))
last <- dose_times[8]
recovery <- lapply(c("MEP", "MPP", "CMP"), function(v) {
  b <- sim_rec[[v]][1]
  after <- sim_rec[sim_rec$time > last, ]
  t_nadir <- after$time[which.min(after[[v]])]
  t80 <- after$time[after$time > t_nadir & after[[v]] >= 0.8 * b][1]
  data.frame(output = v, days_from_last_dose_to_80pct = (t80 - last) / 24)
}) |> bind_rows()
recovery$paper_days <- c(12, 30, 50)
knitr::kable(recovery, digits = 1, caption = "Recovery to 80% of baseline after the eighth dose.")
```

The packaged model recovers in the same order as the paper (MEP, then MPP,
then CMP) but more slowly; with the reference level unstated, the numbers are
not directly comparable.

# Rat single cycle (Figure S1)

Figure S1 shows one cycle at 30 mg/kg; all populations but neutrophils and
monocytes return to baseline.

```{r figS1}
ev_s1 <- rbind(dose_rows(0, 30), obs_rows(seq(0, 40 * 24, by = 4)))
sim_s1 <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod_rat, ev_s1))
sim_s1 |>
  select(time, all_of(outputs)) |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "output", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(output) |>
  mutate(rel = value / first(value), output = factor(output, levels = outputs)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, rel)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 2) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~output, ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Relative to baseline",
       caption = "Replicates Figure S1 of Fornari 2019 (30 mg/kg single dose).")
```

# Human translation (Figure 4)

Figure 4 simulates two 21-day cycles with the Calvert dose for an AUC of
5 mg*min/mL and a GFR of 125 mL/min: 5 x (125 + 25) = 750 mg. The infusion
length is not stated; a 30-minute infusion (as in Zandvliet 2008) is used.
Panel (b) uses the IC50-scaled slopes packaged in
`Fornari_2019_carboplatin_human`; panel (a) uses the rat slopes, applied here
by overriding the three slope parameters.

```{r fig4}
ev_hum <- rbind(dose_rows(c(0, 504), 750, rate = 1500), obs_rows(seq(0, 42 * 24, by = 6)))
sim_b <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod_hum, ev_hum)) |> mutate(slopes = "(b) IC50-scaled slopes")
sim_a <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod_hum, ev_hum,
  params = c(slope_mpp = 2.05, slope_cmp = 1.47, slope_mep = 2.19)
)) |> mutate(slopes = "(a) rat slopes")

# Median lines of Figure 4b, digitised by the maintainers.
fig4b <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(output = "ANC",
             day = c(2.7, 5.1, 7.1, 9.0, 11.2, 14.9, 17.1, 19.8, 21.2, 23.2, 25.2, 27.1, 29.3, 34.9, 37.4, 39.6, 41.0),
             value = c(4.22, 3.86, 3.38, 2.89, 2.65, 2.59, 2.71, 3.09, 3.16, 3.46, 3.46, 3.16, 2.71, 2.37, 2.59, 2.83, 2.96)),
  data.frame(output = "PLT",
             day = c(9.0, 11.2, 13.4, 15.1, 17.1, 19.0, 23.2, 33.9, 37.1),
             value = c(212, 177, 173, 177, 181, 212, 277, 148, 162))
)

bind_rows(sim_a, sim_b) |>
  select(time, slopes, ANC, PLT) |>
  pivot_longer(c(ANC, PLT), names_to = "output", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, value)) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = slopes)) +
  geom_point(data = fig4b, aes(day, value), shape = 1) +
  geom_hline(data = data.frame(output = c("ANC", "ANC", "PLT", "PLT"), y = c(1, 0.5, 50, 25)),
             aes(yintercept = y), linetype = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~output, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "10^9 cells/L", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Open circles: Figure 4b median (digitised). Dotted: grade 3/4 thresholds. Replicates Figure 4 of Fornari 2019.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

cmp4 <- fig4b |>
  mutate(time = round(day * 4) * 6) |>
  inner_join(
    sim_b |> select(time, ANC, PLT) |> pivot_longer(c(ANC, PLT), names_to = "output", values_to = "model"),
    by = c("output", "time")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model / value - 1))
cmp4 |>
  group_by(output) |>
  summarise(median_pct_diff = median(pct_diff), max_abs_pct_diff = max(abs(pct_diff)), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical-value model vs the Figure 4b median line.")

stopifnot(
  # The neutrophil course is driven by the human MTT, kcirc and IC50-scaled
  # slopes; a wrong slope or baseline moves the whole curve.
  abs(median(cmp4$pct_diff[cmp4$output == "ANC"])) < 10,
  quantile(abs(cmp4$pct_diff[cmp4$output == "ANC"]), 0.9) < 20,
  # First-cycle platelet nadir (days 9-19): typical value vs a population median.
  abs(median(cmp4$pct_diff[cmp4$output == "PLT" & cmp4$day < 20])) < 30
)
```

The neutrophil course matches Figure 4b closely. Platelets match in timing
and in the first-cycle nadir to within about 20%; the Figure 4b median falls
further in the second cycle than the typical-value model does. The paper's
bands come from 1,000 simulated patients whose source of variability is not
described, and a median over such a population need not equal the
typical-value trajectory.

# PKNCA: free carboplatin exposure

The paper reports no NCA. The human simulation is checked against the
Calvert target that set the dose: an AUC of 5 mg*min/mL of free carboplatin,
which is 5 x 1000 / 60 / 371.25 x 1000 = 224.5 uM*h. The rat 20 and 30 mg/kg
single doses of Figure S3 are summarised alongside.

```{r pknca}
# Single 30-minute infusion, sampled densely over 72 h (more than 15
# half-lives), solved with tight tolerances so the far tail is not integrator
# noise.
ev_h1 <- rbind(dose_rows(0, 750, rate = 1500), obs_rows(seq(0, 72, by = 0.25)))
sim_h1 <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod_hum, ev_h1, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12))
stopifnot(all(sim_h1$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim_h1$Cc)))
conc_h <- sim_h1 |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  transmute(id = 1L, time, Cc = pmax(Cc, 0), treatment = "human 750 mg")
conc_r <- sim_pk |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  transmute(id = as.integer(id) + 1L, time, Cc, treatment)
conc_all <- bind_rows(conc_h, conc_r)
dose_all <- data.frame(
  id = c(1L, 2L, 3L), time = 0, amt = c(750, 20, 30),
  treatment = c("human 750 mg", "20 mg/kg", "30 mg/kg")
)
nca <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(
  PKNCAconc(conc_all, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCAdose(dose_all, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
nca_tab |>
  rename("Cmax (uM)" = cmax, "AUC0-inf (uM*h)" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 (h)" = half.life) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "PKNCA summary of simulated free carboplatin / platinum.")

cmp_nca <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca,
  reference = data.frame(treatment = "human 750 mg", aucinf.obs = 224.5),
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "uM*h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_nca, caption = "Human AUC vs the Calvert target. * differs by >20%.")
```

The human AUC is about 25% above the Calvert target because the Zandvliet
2008 clearance at a creatinine clearance of 125 mL/min (7.2 L/h) is lower
than the 150 mL/min (9 L/h) the Calvert formula assumes. Fornari et al. do
not say which creatinine clearance they used for the Zandvliet clearance; see
Assumptions and deviations.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Rat dose units and the dose-to-concentration conversion.** Table S3 gives
  the PK volumes in L and clearances in L/h (labelled `1/h` in the table and
  `liter/hour` in the model code); the published model code ends before the
  dosing and unit-conversion lines. The packaged model takes the dose in
  mg/kg, treats the volumes and clearances as per kg (0.26 L/kg and
  0.42 L/h/kg are typical of an extracellular volume and a rat glomerular
  filtration rate), and converts mg/L to uM with the carboplatin molar mass,
  371.25 g/mol. This reproduces the plotted 30 mg/kg free-platinum
  observations of Figure S3, every model line of Figure 3, and the >95%
  reticulocyte nadir. The plotted PK and damage lines of Figure S3 are about
  1.5-fold higher than this at every time; using the platinum atomic mass
  (195.08 g/mol, a 1.9-fold increase) instead would deepen the MPP and MEP
  nadirs below those of Figure 3, so the carboplatin molar mass is kept.
- **Red blood cell equation.** Equation 9 lists only neutrophils, monocytes,
  reticulocytes and platelets, although red blood cells are a model output
  with their own circulating rate and residual error. The packaged model uses
  `d/dt(RBC) = kcircRet * Ret - kcircRBC * RBC`, the balance implied by the
  steady-state relation `kcircRet = kcircRBC * RBC0 / Ret0` of Equation S4.
- **Typographical errors in Equations 4 and 7.** The second line of
  Equation 4 is printed as `dCMP/dt` but is the MEP equation. Equation 7
  prints the outflow of the first platelet transit compartment as
  `aRet * T1Plt`; the packaged model uses `aPlt * T1Plt`, which is what the
  steady-state derivation of `kprolPlt` and `ktrPlt` (Equation S4) requires.
  With `aRet` the system would not be at steady state without drug.
- **Feedback weights.** Equations 11-13 use weights of 1/2; the published
  model code sets `alphaWBC = 0.5`. The model code defines one damage rate,
  `kdamage = 0.017`; Table 1 lists `kdam` and `krep` as 0.017 1/h each, and
  both are used.
- **Number of rat cycles.** Table S1 lists seven 40 mg/kg doses for study E,
  but Figure 3 shows eight cycles and the text refers to eight; eight are
  simulated.
- **Free-platinum observations.** The PK was fitted separately (Phoenix NLME,
  naive pooled, multiplicative error whose magnitude is not reported), so the
  packaged models expose `Cc` but carry no residual error for it.
- **Human baselines given as ranges.** Table 1 prints normal ranges for human
  Neut0 (2-7), Mono0 (0.2-10), Ret0 (40-115) and RBC0 (4,100-5,900) x 10^9/L.
  The maintainers used the midpoints. The Figure 4 neutrophil median starts at
  about 4.5, the Neut0 midpoint. The Mono0 range is read as 0.2-1.0 (normal
  adult monocyte counts; an upper limit of 10 x 10^9/L would be a marked
  monocytosis), giving 0.6.
- **Human slopes.** Equation 10 scales each rat slope by the ratio of rat to
  human IC50s (Table S2: CMP 2.83 vs 4.04 uM, MEP 0.86 vs 1.56 uM), which would
  give SlopeCMP = 1.03 and SlopeMEP = 1.21 1/uM. Table 2 prints 0.57 and
  0.66, and 0.79 for MPP (no MPP IC50 is reported). The printed values equal
  the rat slope times the product of the CMP and MEP ratios for MPP and CMP,
  and times the square of the MEP ratio for MEP. The printed Table 2 values
  are used; they reproduce the Figure 4b neutrophil course.
- **Figure 4a.** With the rat slopes the packaged human model predicts more
  neutropenia than with the IC50-scaled slopes, as larger slopes must. The
  published Figure 4a and 4c show less neutropenia with the rat slopes; the
  paper does not explain this, and it is not reproduced.
- **Human PK.** Supplementary Text S11 uses the Zandvliet 2008 free-carboplatin
  model (packaged as `Zandvliet_2008_carboplatin`) without stating the
  covariates. The packaged human model uses its typical values with
  CL = 0.76 x CLcr + 1.5 L/h at CLcr = 125 mL/min (7.5 L/h), the GFR that
  Supplementary Text S11 assumes for the Calvert dose, giving 7.2 L/h; this
  gives an AUC of 6.25 rather than 5 mg*min/mL. The PK IIV of Zandvliet 2008 is
  not carried. Concentrations are converted to uM with the carboplatin molar
  mass so that the damage drive is on the scale of the uM-based slopes.
- **Human residual error.** No human residual error is reported. The rat
  Table S4 values are carried into the human model, as the paper does for
  every human parameter it did not rescale; they describe rat assay and
  between-animal scatter, not human variability.
- **Human population variability.** Figure 4 shows bands from 1,000 simulated
  patients, but the paper does not say which parameters varied. The packaged
  human model has no IIV, so only typical-value trajectories are compared.
- **Recovery times.** The Results text gives recovery times to 80% of the
  original population after the last cycle without stating the reference time
  or level; the packaged model's times are reported without a gate.
- Europe PMC lists no erratum, correction or retraction for this article as
  of 2026-11-26.
